skill.name: defuddle
skill.description: Extract clean Markdown from web pages with Defuddle CLI, removing navigation, ads, and clutter before analysis.
skill.summary: Clean web pages into Markdown with Defuddle CLI for focused reading and analysis.
skill.author: kepano

security_audit.summary: The static findings are mostly Markdown backtick false positives, but several examples do instruct external CLI execution. The confirmed risks are expected for this skill, yet they still require careful handling of package installation, user-supplied URLs, and file output.

remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before installing Defuddle globally, and document the trusted package source or a pinned version.

remediation.issue: User-supplied URL passed to a CLI command
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to validate and quote URLs before command execution, especially when URLs contain shell metacharacters.

remediation.issue: File output example may overwrite local content
remediation.suggestion: Advise users to choose an explicit safe output path and check for existing files before saving extracted content.

content.value_statement: Web pages often include navigation, ads, and scripts that waste model context. This skill uses Defuddle CLI to extract clean Markdown for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Runs Defuddle CLI examples for parsing a supplied URL into Markdown.
Shows how to save extracted content to a local Markdown file.
Shows metadata extraction for title, description, and domain fields.
Documents output choices for Markdown, JSON, HTML, and property values.
Positions Defuddle as an alternative to WebFetch for standard pages.
limitations: Requires the Defuddle CLI to be installed before use.
Works only on URLs that Defuddle can access and parse successfully.
Does not define validation for unsafe or malformed URL strings.
Does not handle login-only pages, paywalls, or JavaScript-heavy sites by itself.

use_cases.title: Summarize Articles
use_cases.description: Extract clean article text before summarizing, quoting, or comparing source claims.

use_cases.title: Read Documentation
use_cases.description: Convert documentation pages into focused Markdown before asking technical questions.

use_cases.title: Capture Page Metadata
use_cases.description: Extract titles, descriptions, and domains for source review or content inventories.

prompt_templates.title: Read a Web Article
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Defuddle to extract clean Markdown from this URL, then give me a concise summary: [URL]

prompt_templates.title: Compare Documentation Pages
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract clean Markdown from these two documentation URLs with Defuddle, then list the key differences: [URL 1], [URL 2]

prompt_templates.title: Capture Source Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Defuddle to extract the title, description, and domain from this URL, then explain whether it fits my research task: [URL]

prompt_templates.title: Build a Source Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Defuddle for each URL in this source list, save clean content when helpful, and produce a source-by-source brief: [URLs]

output_examples.input: A user provides a news article URL and asks for a summary.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns the article text without page clutter, then summarizes the main points and source metadata.

output_examples.input: A user asks whether two documentation pages describe the same API behavior.
output_examples.output: The assistant extracts both pages, compares the clean content, and reports matching details, differences, and open questions.

output_examples.input: A user wants title and description metadata for a source list.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns the requested metadata for each page and highlights sources that need manual review.

best_practices: Use Markdown output when the next step is reading, summarizing, or comparing page content.
Review the cleaned content before making claims about source details.
Treat every URL as untrusted input and quote or validate it before command execution.
anti_patterns: Do not pass suspicious URL strings into a shell command without validation.
Do not use this skill for pages that require private credentials unless the user explicitly provides access.
Do not assume extracted text preserves every interactive element or script-rendered detail.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps an assistant use Defuddle CLI to extract clean Markdown from web pages.

faq.question: Does it replace WebFetch?
faq.answer: It can be a better choice for standard pages because it removes navigation and clutter.

faq.question: Does it install Defuddle automatically?
faq.answer: No. It shows an installation command, but installation depends on the user or environment.

faq.question: Can it save extracted content?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions include an example for saving clean Markdown to a local file.

faq.question: Can it read private or login-only pages?
faq.answer: Not by itself. Defuddle can only parse pages that the environment can access.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The generated report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
